candidates.title: Design and mechanical analysis of the PRAGYA tokamak vacuum vessel
candidates.notes: Accessible peer-reviewed preprint (March 12, 2026) by Shaurya Kaushal et al. Provides first published machine parameters for PRAGYA: R0≈0.4 m, a>0.18 m, Ip up to 25 kA, B_T=0.1 T. Structural FEM analysis of vacuum vessel under atmospheric pressure, thermal, and self-weight loads. Does not describe JENGA directly, but is the first substantive published technical document from Pranos. Establishes machine geometry for the experimental PRAGYA device (not the commercial 50 MW vision).

candidates.title: Why we invested in Pranos Fusion — Ankur Capital
candidates.notes: Investor rationale post. Confirms '20+ Tesla HTS magnets' (resolving gap 3 — magnet type — as HTS confirmed). Describes JENGA as microsecond-level plasma control software. No machine parameters or JENGA output data. Qualitative only. Not extracted — no quantitative data warranting extraction as a standalone source.

candidates.title: Pranos Nets $6.8 Mn To Build Tokamak, Superconducting Magnets For Nuclear Fusion — inc42
candidates.notes: News article on Series A round ($6.8M from pi Ventures, Ankur Capital, Industrial47, Groww co-founder, Razorpay founders, Bhukhanwala Industries). Analysis currently records only $417K seed — this is a major update. PRAGYA described as 'not suitable for actual fusion' (experimental testing device only). JENGA described as likely first revenue product. Not extracted — no quantitative technical data beyond funding figures.

candidates.title: India-based Fusion Tech Startup Pranos Raises $6.8 Million — ESG Today

extracted.notes: Extracted to iter-02/sources/arxiv-2603-11549.md. Peer-reviewed preprint; first published technical document from Pranos Fusion. Provides PRAGYA machine geometry (R0≈0.4 m, a>0.18 m) — critical for analysis sections S1/S2/S5 even though PRAGYA is an experimental device, not the 50 MW commercial concept.

entries.analyst_notes: Gap 14 specifically targets Jenga digital twin validation outputs. No JENGA-specific preprint or model output was found. The arXiv paper addresses vacuum vessel structural design (FEM), not JENGA simulation outputs. However, it is the only published technical document from Pranos Fusion and provides machine parameters for PRAGYA (R0=0.4 m) which incidentally helps anchor several other blocking gaps (G-1 machine geometry, G-3 magnet type via Ankur Capital confirmation). Gap 14 remains open in the strict sense — no JENGA model outputs have been published as of April 2026.

candidates.title: Pranos Fusion — Company Website
candidates.notes: Accessible HTML (not JS-blocked). Confirms Jenga as 'tokamak design and plasma-control software' that 'integrates control-oriented design from the outset'. Critically, states JENGA and PRAGYA are 'engineered to integrate HTS magnet modules' — first public confirmation of HTS magnet route. No simulation outputs or validated model results published. Also documents MAGGA as HTS magnet sub-program.

candidates.title: Pranos Nets $6.8 Mn To Build Tokamak, Superconducting Magnets For Nuclear Fusion — inc42
candidates.notes: Full article content accessible. Documents $6.8M Series A round (March 24, 2026), lead investors pi Ventures and Ankur Capital, with participation from Industrial47, Lalit Keshre (Groww co-founder), Razorpay founders, Bhukhanwala Industries. Describes three-part stack: JENGA (design/control software), PRAGYA (tokamak platform), MAGGA (HTS magnet program). States JENGA is 'likely to convert into a revenue making product soon' with 'pilot level integration expected within a year'. First tokamak commissioning targeted for 2026. Significant update to analysis — prior funding was $417K seed; now $6.8M total.

candidates.notes: Same funding round covered in inc42 article. Describes Pranos as 'high-field fusion reactor technology'. Confirms MAGGA HTS magnet program. No additional technical content beyond inc42 article; skipped extraction to preserve budget.

extracted.notes: Confirms HTS magnet integration (MAGGA program) — partial resolution of G-3. No Jenga simulation outputs present.

Documents $6.8M funding round (March 24, 2026). Significant update to analysis funding section. Provides clearest public description of Jenga as plasma-control software (not just simulation/digital twin). No model outputs.

entries.notes: No published Jenga simulation outputs or digital twin validation results found across all searches. G-14 remains open. The Jenga platform is now better characterized as 'design and plasma-control software' (not solely a digital twin) — the IAEA FUSE profile's description of MHD/transport/neutronics/thermal-structural modules appears to be aspirational rather than validated. Two high-value ancillary sources were extracted: (1) company website confirming HTS magnet route via MAGGA program; (2) $6.8M funding round article (March 2026) with product stack detail. These address other analysis gaps (G-3 magnet type, funding accuracy) even though G-14 (Jenga validation outputs) remains unresolved.
